The infrared science technology interest group will hold its next seminar on Tuesday at 2 p.m. Eastern time, hosted virtually. The session will feature two presentations on advances in detector arrays for future astrophysics missions, followed by a moderated discussion. Topics will include progress on large-format sensors, strategies for reducing noise in cryogenic systems, and lessons learned from recent flight programs. The seminar is open to researchers, engineers, students, and members of the public with an interest in the topic. Registration is not required, but participants are encouraged to submit questions in advance using the form on the group's web page. A recording will be posted within one week of the event, along with slides provided by the speakers. Questions about the series may be directed to the group's coordinator.
